activities.anchor: the modern user is the flat on a 125-year lease
activities.caption: pair each holding with what it really is
activities.name: propEstateMatch

config.prompt: Nobody owns land outright — pair each holding with its true shape:

pairs.right: the nearest thing to ownership — indefinite, transferable, bequeathable
a term of years carved out, coexisting with the landlord's reversion
until death — with remainders and reversions ripening later
a permission only — revocable, no estate

config.why: The Crown owns all land; everyone else holds an estate — and a lease is itself an estate that can be sold, mortgaged and underlet.

activities.anchor: the universal test of a functioning property system
activities.caption: file each layer of the land system
activities.name: propInterestsBuckets

config.prompt: Around the estate, three layers orbit — file each:

items.label: easements — rights of way, drainage, light through defined windows
freehold covenants — maintain a fence, pay estate charges
the Land Registration Act 2002's register-as-everything logic
the mirror, curtain and insurance principles
compulsory purchase, against compensation plus disturbance

config.why: Registration replaced the chain-of-deeds archaeology with a state-guaranteed register — and most "homeowners" co-own their title with a bank for decades.

config.prompt: Open, exclusive, unpermitted occupation of unregistered land — how many years before the possessor can acquire title?
config.why: Twelve — the logic is diligence over dormancy, and stale claims die. Registered land now gives the owner notice and two years to object, defanging the surprise.
config.context: A century's quiet policy dispute — certainty of registered title versus the sleeping-owner penalty — settled by procedure.

activities.anchor: the freeholder's reversion under your lease — is not yours at all
activities.caption: bet on the absolute owner
activities.name: propAbsolutePredict

config.q: A buyer exclaims: "It's mine — my land, my rules." Which of these can override that claim?
choices: Planning law, utilities' statutory access, neighbours' easements and nuisance claims, compulsory purchase, taxing powers — and the reversion under your lease
config.why: Every ownership is already relative: ownership is a legal allocation, continuously renegotiated — not a natural absolute.

activities.caption: pair each IP right with its term logic
activities.name: propIPMatch

config.prompt: Four settlements of one trade-off — pair the right with its duration logic:

pairs.right: society needs to build on inventions, so the monopoly is short and conditional
expression protected, with fair-dealing keeping the commons usable
brand goodwill is a continuing investment, and deception never expires
protected as long as they stay secret — where the disclosure price is too high

config.why: Novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability test patents; the idea-expression dichotomy is copyright's load-bearing wall.

config.prompt: Once invented, what does it cost a competitor to copy the drug in the worked example?
config.why: £20m to copy against £800m to develop — non-rival and public-good-like: imitators race to marginal cost and nothing recovers development, which is why the time-capped monopoly is the deliberate price of disclosure.
config.context: Generic competition on expiry is the designed payoff — every IP policy argument renegotiates this arithmetic's terms.

activities.caption: find the line the label-worshipper wrote
activities.name: propLeaseSpot

config.prompt: One line of this leases summary is wrong — click it:
lines: Essentials (Street v Mountford): exclusive possession, for a term, at a rent.
Sham "licences" are leases if the substance matches — the exceptions are genuine service occupancy.
Tenant covenants (repair, use) bind assignees of the burden.
Landlord covenants die on any sale of the reversion.
Security-of-tenure statutes overlay the contract with protection.
config.correction: Landlord covenants (quiet enjoyment, non-derogation from grant) bind the reversion too — covenants run both ways.
config.why: England's leasehold houses and the commonhold alternative are the structural disputes — a lease allocates risk across time and persons.

activities.caption: walk the purchase past the register
activities.name: propRegisterOrder

config.prompt: A registered-land purchase, step by step — order the walk:
items: Obtain official copies — property, proprietorship and charges registers
Read the title class — absolute title is the state's guarantee to the stated extent
Rely on the mirror — the register reflects title
Trust the curtain — equitable interests behind trusts stay off it
Bank the insurance — the state indemnifies losses from register errors
config.why: Overriding interests — actual occupation, short leases, easements by long use — are the documented exceptions, and the 2002 Act's direction is to shrink them so the mirror reflects.
